title: POC: traffic scaling & token-skew modeling — Wildcard AI
summary: POC scoping focused on building a traffic model that captures Wildcard's heavy token-skew (many short prompt-only calls plus a small % of very long generation), defining success criteria (latency SLOs, throughput targets, quality guardrails), and aligning on bench plan and timeline for a 3-week pilot starting late Nov. Action owners and artifact links agreed.
topics: token distribution: short vs mid vs long generations
benchmark plan: synthetic load + replay of real traces
deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC/private
cost/throughput tradeoffs, batching and caching config
action_items: Maya Chen: share traffic-model spreadsheet and example trace (due: 2025-11-10)
Devon Patel: prepare initial benchmark plan with parameterized QPS/concurrency scenarios (due: 2025-11-12)
Liam O'Connor: export 48h anonymized request logs and token histograms, mark PII fields (due: 2025-11-09)
Priya Kapoor: confirm procurement/PO timeline and internal pilot stakeholders (due: 2025-11-14)
next_steps: Redwood to run a baseline micro-benchmark using Wildcard sample trace and share p50/p95/p99 latency curves
Customer to validate token-skew numbers and provide 1 week of production traces (anonymized)
Schedule pilot kick-off: propose 2025-11-24 for environment setup and bench run during Thanksgiving week window
Agree on success criteria doc: latency SLOs, quality checks, cost targets
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-05 15:00 PT / Duration 54m / Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Wildcard Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (Wildcard ML Eng), Sofia Ramos (Wildcard CTO)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call — i see priya, liam, sofia — can you hear me okay?
[00:04] Priya: yep, loud and clear. thanks Maya.
[00:07] Devon: hi all. i'll be the technical lead on the redwood side for the benchmarks.
[00:11] Sofia: thanks, yeah we wanted to get concrete today on how our traffic shape maps to your capacity planning and what success looks like.
[00:16] Maya: great. real quick agenda — characterize workload (qps, concurrency, token mix), define success criteria (latency, quality, cost), and agree bench plan and timeline. sound good?
[00:23] Priya: yep. please note we have strict audit requirements — SOC2 logs and kvm keys for anything that touches prod data.
[00:30] Devon: absolutely, we'll note that under the security/ops section, you can opt for private or dedicated.

[00:45] Topic: Workload overview
[00:47] Liam: quick background: Wildcard runs a user-facing assistant embedded in our editor — most calls are short completions: single-shot rewriting, classification hooks; then we have a smaller fraction of long creative generations for content generation. overall request volume averages 120 QPS during business hours with peaks to roughly 480 QPS for a few minutes during product events.
[01:05] Maya: 120 sustained, 480 peak — helpful. what's your concurrency (simultaneous in-flight requests)?
[01:10] Liam: on average ~90 concurrent active requests, peaks up to ~350.
[01:15] Devon: okay that concurrency: qps ratio suggests average request latency in the 200-600ms range historically?
[01:20] Liam: sort of — but our token mix skews things. about 60% of calls are tiny: prompt-only or 1-20 output tokens, 30% are mid-size 50-250 tokens, and 10% are long >500 tokens, sometimes up to 2k tokens. The long ones are rare but drive GPU time and make p99 awful.
[01:38] Priya: we measured token histograms last quarter, i'll share them.
[01:42] Maya: that distribution is super useful. for benching we typically capture 3 scenarios: short-heavy, mid-mix, and worst-case tail. we'll parameterize traffic model by qps, concurrency target, and token mix.

[02:05] Topic: Success criteria discussion
[02:07] Maya: let's put numbers. what SLOs do you need? p95 and p99 are typical.
[02:11] Sofia: p95 should be below 450ms for the short + mid requests — our UX team says anything above that feels laggy. for long gens we can accept higher latency but want predictable service: p95 < 3s for >500 token outputs and p99 < 8s.
[02:27] Devon: sounds reasonable. we'll test both p95/p99 and tail variability. Another success metric customers use is cost per 1M tokens under the pilot profile. do you have a target?
[02:36] Priya: we'd like to see at least 30% improvement vs our current infra cost, or a clear path with batching/caching to that number.
[02:42] Liam: quality guardrail: identical or better Rouge/bertscore for our generation tests; also no regressions on our proprietary eval prompts.
[02:50] Maya: noted: latency, cost delta, and quality parity.

[03:10] Topic: Traffic modeling details
[03:12] Devon: for the traffic model we'll ask for: 48h traces with timestamps, request ids, input token counts, output token counts, and success/failure flags. if you can't share raw logs, a token histogram and inter-arrival distribution will work.
[03:24] Liam: we can provide anonymized traces; we'll strip PII. what's the ideal granularity for timestamps?
[03:29] Devon: millisecond-level is best but second-level is ok for initial modeling. we also want to know event-driven bursts — e.g., a product notification time where many requests hit concurrently.
[03:38] Priya: that's our biggest complexity — scheduled campaigns cause short 30–90s bursts to triple qps.
[03:44] Maya: we'll model both steady-state and burst scenarios. for bursts we model ramp-up time and peak sustain duration — the backend routing and warm pools matter here.

[04:05] Topic: Bench plan and benchmarks to run
[04:08] Devon: our bench plan: 1) replay of your anonymized trace against candidate model variants (open weights + quantized versions), 2) synthetic scenarios to sweep QPS and concurrency, 3) controlled tail tests that push only the 10% long-gen traffic to measure p99. We'll collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory pressure, and cost estimate (tokens * compute seconds).
[04:31] Sofia: will you include prefix caching and KV cache behaviors? Our assistant often reuses context across requests.
[04:36] Devon: yes — we'll simulate prefix/KV caching options; in some runs we enable short prefix cache (for repeated prompts) and in others disable it to measure worst-case. note the transcriptions sometimes call it "kay-v cache" in our notes — same thing.

[05:00] Priya: what's your expected runway for a pilot — how long to stand up environments and run benches?
[05:05] Maya: typical pilot is 2–3 weeks: week 1 environment + trace ingestion, week 2 bench runs and optimization, week 3 result validation and a short follow-up. we can compress if we get traces and accounts fast.
[05:15] Priya: we have a procurement window in late nov so the 3-week pilot starting 2025-11-24 works for us.
[05:21] Maya: i'll put tentative dates in calendar.

[05:35] Topic: Model variants and fallbacks
[05:37] Devon: we'll test a primary model (your tuned 13B) vs a cost-optimized quantized 13B and an alternative 7B for lower-latency short completions. Redwood supports routing by policy so we can route short completion traffic to the fast 7B when quality metrics pass.
[05:53] Liam: that routing is interesting; does it add additional latency?
[05:56] Devon: negligible at the gateway level — the bigger effect is model warmness and KV cache compatibility. we need compatible tokenizer and KV cache semantics.

[06:10] Topic: Data protection and compliance
[06:12] Priya: SOC2 and audit logs are mandatory — any bench that uses production-like traces must be in a private/dedicated environment with KMS controls.
[06:20] Maya: agree. we'll run the bench in a dedicated sandbox provisioned to your tenancy or in your VPC if you prefer. we'll provide an SOC2 artifact and an audit-trail export.

[06:35] Topic: Observability and metrics
[06:37] Devon: we will provide per-route dashboards: token-level breakdown, cost per token, GPU utilization, and latency heatmaps (time-series and percentiles). we'll also record sample outputs for quality evals.
[06:47] Sofia: can you export the raw logs after the bench? we need them for our internal evals.
[06:50] Maya: yes, redwood can provide the raw bench logs and a summarized report.

[07:05] Topic: Cost modeling specifics
[07:08] Devon: cost modeling will include per-token compute seconds times the effective instance cost plus any reserved capacity charge if we use dedicated. we'll produce an apples-to-apples comparison vs your current infra.
[07:18] Priya: remember to include the ops uplift — we need to compare TCO including runbook maintenance.

[07:35] Cross-talk and clarifications
[07:36] Liam: so for short-heavy traffic do you recommend batching?
[07:38] Devon: for sub-50-token outputs batching can help but increases tail for very low-latency paths. we typically use small batch windows (5–15ms) and dynamic batching to balance p95 and throughput. if you need ultra-low p95 < 200ms, we might prefer model routing to a low-latency 7B instead of aggressive batching.
[07:58] Priya: ok noted. what about caching?
[08:00] Devon: prefix caching reduces tokens/sec and cost for repeated prompts; combined with routing it can yield >20% cost savings in short-heavy workloads.

[08:15] Topic: Acceptance criteria recap
[08:17] Maya: recapping: 1) p95 < 450ms for short+mid under pilot profile, 2) p95 < 3s for long gens and stable p99 behavior, 3) quality parity on your eval suite, 4) cost improvement >=30% or a clear optimization path. any edits?
[08:32] Sofia: add audit/compliance requirement: bench must run in a dedicated environment with KMS and audit logs.
[08:37] Maya: added.

[08:45] Topic: Risks and mitigation
[08:47] Devon: main risk is token-skew tail causing p99 degradation — we'll test targeted tail loads and propose routing/fallback rules. another risk is workload-dependent kernel performance; we'll run multi-sequence length kernel sweeps.
[09:02] Priya: also procurement friction — we'll need a short MSA amendment for pilot if we touch prod traces.

[09:15] Closing and next steps
[09:16] Maya: action items: we'll share the model template + spreadsheet and set up a secure S3 drop for traces. Devon will draft the bench plan. Priya and Liam to provide traces and confirm procurement timing.
[09:28] Priya: sounds good. thanks team.
[09:31] Sofia: thanks, bye.
[09:33] Maya: bye everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the spreadsheet.

Notes: transcription contains small mis-hearings ("kay-v" for KV, sometimes the model name typed as "wild-card 13B"), filler words present. Links / artifacts referenced: https://redwood.ai/pilot-templates (deck), https://s3.redwood.example/wildcard-traffic-model (placeholder link to be created by Maya).
